query_snapshot: What corrosion mechanism does NBS Circular 592 associate with hydrochloric acid and other halide-containing solutions attacking stainless steel?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NBS Circular 592 states that hydrochloric acid and other halide-containing solutions attack the passive film on stainless steel. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 60-61, chunk e035b4b6; nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485]
- NBS Circular 592 states that attack by hydrochloric acid and other halide-containing solutions produces corrosion of the pitting type on stainless steel. [nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 60-61, chunk e035b4b6; nbscircular592.pdf, pp. 59-60, chunk b0a15485]
